text: Correct: `∃ x, Transcendental k x ∧ FiniteDimensional k⟮x⟯ F` says that F is finite over a rational subfield, exactly the one-variable definition in [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Quantifying over x makes the predicate independent of a chosen parameter. The [comparison with Mathlib’s `FunctionField`](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L131) supplies the same condition when an embedding of `RatFunc k` is fixed. No perfectness, finite base field, separability, or exact-constants assumption belongs in this definition. The roadmap’s rational and non-exact-constant controls are substantive: [k(x) satisfies the predicate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Basic.lean#L115), while the proof of [ℓ(0)=2 for C(x)/R](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/RealComplex.lean#L28) explicitly constructs `IsFunctionField ℝ (RatFunc ℂ)`. Thus the definition does not silently force the constant field to be exact.
The native rational function field supplies a transcendental generator and finite extension of its generated subfield.
The intrinsic existential definition agrees with Mathlib’s function-field condition for a chosen compatible rational-function embedding.
Its source constructs IsFunctionField R (RatFunc C) and computes the native zero-divisor Riemann–Roch dimension as two, guarding against an implicit exact-constants assumption.

Correct on the documented domain: Lean takes the supremum of `(deg D + 1 − ℓ(D)).toNat`. For function fields the range is bounded; with exact constants the zero divisor has defect zero, so truncation loses nothing and [the supremum is attained](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/Genus.lean#L246). This realizes [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.4.15 and Corollary 1.4.16](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Outside those hypotheses the doc explicitly describes the possible junk value, rather than asserting the classical invariant. The required rational calibration is proved from an [actual polynomial description of L(nP∞)](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/RatFunc.lean#L144): its dimension is n+1 and `genus k (RatFunc k)=0`. The separate [ℓ(0)=2 computation for C(x)/R](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/RealComplex.lean#L28) checks the exact-constants guard. Neither a chosen canonical divisor nor Riemann–Hurwitz is used to define this genus.
Under the explicit function-field and exact-constants hypotheses, a divisor attains the untruncated integer defect equal to genus.
The native Riemann–Roch space on k(x) is computed via polynomials of degree at most n and has dimension n+1, including n=0.
The native supremum definition gives genus zero for the rational function field.
The actual non-exact extension C(x)/R has zero-divisor dimension two, so ℓ(0)=1 cannot be used without exact constants.

Correct: unfolding `WeilDivisor (Place k F)` gives `Place k F →₀ ℤ`, so an element is a finite formal integer sum of normalized places. This matches [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.4.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html); equality is coefficientwise, with no quotient by principal divisors. Negative coefficients and the empty support are retained. The carrier makes sense for arbitrary field extensions, while finite-support assertions about divisors of functions separately require `IsFunctionField`. The roadmap’s concrete controls use this very carrier: [div(x)=P₍X₎−P∞](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Divisor/RatFunc.lean#L85) and [div(X²+1)=P₍X²+1₎−2P∞](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Divisor/RatFunc.lean#L110). Together with the proved residue degrees 1 and 2, these give weighted degree zero. The latter example distinguishes multiplicity two at infinity from merely counting the two places in the support.
The native divisor of X is the finite-support difference of its degree-one zero and infinity, checking signs and coefficients.
For irreducible X²+1, the native principal divisor has coefficient one at its quadratic place and minus two at infinity.
The quadratic place in the preceding actual divisor computation has residue degree two.

Correct: `WeilDivisor.weightedDegree (fun P ↦ P.degree)` expands to the finite sum ΣP D(P)[κ(P):k], with integer coefficients. It is therefore the residue-weighted degree of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.4.1](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html), including negative divisors and degree zero for the empty sum. Finite residue degree is supplied under `IsFunctionField`; the raw `finrank` definition also has its documented meaning outside that domain. The [X²+1 divisor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Divisor/RatFunc.lean#L110) and [degree-two residue calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/XSqAddOne.lean#L58) give 1·2−2·1=0 over Q. Counting coefficients without residue weights would give −1, so this genuinely tests the convention. The [X divisor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Divisor/RatFunc.lean#L85) similarly gives 1−1=0. These are compositions of existing proved computations, not newly claimed standalone numerical lemmas.
The weighted divisor-degree homomorphism evaluates a point divisor to its residue degree.
The actual quadratic principal divisor has coefficients one and minus two, providing the non-rational-place weighting test.
The quadratic zero place has residue degree two, so its contribution is two rather than one.
Infinity contributes residue degree one in both rational principal-divisor calculations.
Under IsFunctionField, every native principal divisor has weighted degree zero; the inspected proof separately handles algebraic functions.

Correct: `P.valuation.valuationSubring` is the actual subring of F defined by vP(f)≤1, hence the valuation ring of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.4](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). The place’s surjectivity supplies a nontrivial discrete valuation, while triviality on k embeds every constant in this ring. With Lean’s sign convention the [membership criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L256) is ordP(f)≥0; zero is included even though its integer-valued order is the documented junk value zero. This is checked concretely at infinity: [x is outside the ring exactly at P∞](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Basic.lean#L360), and [x⁻¹ has order one there](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Basic.lean#L140). Thus the construction detects poles and regular functions in the roadmap’s rational-place control. It does not assume F/k is a function field or confuse this local valuation ring with a global ring of integers.
The multiplicative valuation-subring construction agrees with the additive nonnegative-order criterion, including zero.
In the native rational function field X fails to be integral precisely at the place at infinity.
The inverse rational coordinate has order one at infinity, so it is an actual uniformizer in the selected valuation ring.

Correct: `Module.finrank k P.ResidueField` measures the residue extension over the specified constants, matching [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.14](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). `ResidueField` is the quotient of the actual valuation ring by its maximal ideal. The definition’s warning about `finrank` is substantive: [finite-dimensionality and positivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Degree.lean#L226) are proved under `IsFunctionField`, without a finite or perfect constant-field assumption. The roadmap controls are present: [infinity has degree one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Basic.lean#L210), and polynomial places have degree `natDegree`. For X²+1, [the source proves degree two and constructs the residue equivalence with k(i)](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/XSqAddOne.lean#L58); its defining equation sends the residue of X to i. Specializing to Q gives the prescribed non-rational place, rather than silently treating every closed point as degree one.
The function-field hypothesis makes the native residue field finite-dimensional over k, eliminating finrank’s infinite-dimensional junk case.
Every place of an actual function field has positive residue degree.
The native infinity place on k(x) has degree one.
An irreducible polynomial place has residue degree equal to the polynomial’s natural degree.
The actual irreducible quadratic-place calibration computes residue degree two.
The native residue-field equivalence sends the class of X to i, identifying the quadratic residue field as k(i), and in particular Q(i).

Correct with its explicit zero convention: `Valuation.ord` is −log of the multiplicative valuation, so zeros have positive order, poles negative order, and a uniformizer order one. On nonzero elements this is the normalized order of [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.12](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html). Lean extends it to zero by `ord 0=0`, not infinity; the documentation says so, and [multiplicativity requires both factors nonzero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Basic.lean#L171). The roadmap’s sign check is direct: [ord∞(f)=−intDegree(f)](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/RatFunc/Basic.lean#L128) gives ord∞(x)=−1, while the source separately proves ord∞(x⁻¹)=1. The [native principal divisor of x](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Divisor/RatFunc.lean#L85) is P₍X₎−P∞, confirming the same convention globally. Thus the integer codomain’s junk at zero does not enter the function-divisor or nonzero valuation laws.
The total integer-valued order deliberately returns zero at the zero field element, as documented.
Order is additive on multiplication of two nonzero elements; the required guards are present.
The native infinity place computes order as minus rational-function degree, yielding order minus one for X.
The native inverse coordinate has order one at infinity, checking normalization.
The principal divisor of X has a positive zero coefficient and a negative infinity coefficient, confirming the order sign in its actual consumer.

Correct: the definition first pulls P′’s valuation back along F→F′, then normalizes its value group to obtain a place of F. The elaborated signature retains `Algebra.IsIntegral F F′`; this ensures the restricted valuation is nontrivial and can be normalized surjectively. The [valuation-ring membership equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Extension/Basic.lean#L383) identifies its ring with the preimage of O(P′), and the following uniqueness theorem gives precisely the place below P′. This is the construction in [Stichtenoth, Definition 3.1.3 and Proposition 3.1.4](https://dokumen.pub/algebraic-function-fields-and-codes-2nbsped-3540768777-9783540768777.html); the doc’s “3.1.2” is a locator error, not a different mathematical claim. The [identity-extension computation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Extension/Basic.lean#L1018) returns P itself. Ramified normalization is also checked by the actual [unique place above infinity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ArtinSchreier/Monomial.lean#L240) in the monomial Artin–Schreier family.
The valuation ring of the restricted normalized place is exactly the inverse image of the original valuation ring.
The place below P′ is uniquely characterized by inclusion of its valuation ring in O(P′).
Normalization of pullback along the identity returns the original normalized place.
The actual monomial Artin–Schreier function field has a unique degree-one place restricting to infinity; restriction is nonvacuously realized in a ramified example.

Correct in the documented algebraic-extension setting: `ordIndex` is the least positive order attained by the pulled-back valuation, hence the scaling index e. The source proves [e>0 and ordP′(f)=e·ordP(f)](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Extension/Basic.lean#L356), agreeing with [Stacks, Tag 09E4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09E4). The raw definition is more general: without algebraicity the restriction may be trivial and `ordIndex` then gives zero; positivity and the normalized restricted place are only asserted with the required hypothesis. The [identity-extension check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Extension/Basic.lean#L1027) gives e=1. A genuine ramified control comes from [the native Artin–Schreier field yᵖ−y=xᵐ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ArtinSchreier/Monomial.lean#L206): the unique place over infinity has e=p. In particular p=2,m=3 gives e=2, so no unramified or tame assumption is hidden in this definition.
Algebraicity of the extension guarantees that the pulled-back valuation has a positive order index.
The native restricted place satisfies the defining order-scaling equation with this ramification index.
The identity extension has ramification index one.
The actual Artin–Schreier monomial field has ramification index p above infinity; specializing p=2,m=3 gives e=2.

Correct: Lean takes the multiplicity of P′’s height-one centre in the different ideal of the integral closure of O(P). Finite separability makes that ideal nonzero, so multiplicity is a genuine finite exponent. Mathlib identifies the ideal with the inverse trace-dual module, matching the [Dedekind different](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BW0) and the doc’s −ord(t) convention. The [prime-power divisibility criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Different/Basic.lean#L227) checks this interpretation directly. The required wild control is substantive: [native monomial formulas](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ArtinSchreier/Monomial.lean#L206) give e=2,d=4 for y²−y=x³ in characteristic two, and the source proves its genus is one. The [y²=x⁵−1 calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Hyperelliptic/Genus/Two.lean#L163) gives different degree six away from characteristics 2 and 5, with finite branch contribution five plus infinity. No assumption of tameness or perfect constants is hidden in the local definition.
The exponent is exactly the largest n for which the centre prime to the nth power divides the actual nonzero different ideal.
Zero different exponent corresponds to genuine Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt, retaining residue separability rather than incorrectly replacing it by e=1.
The actual monomial Artin–Schreier function field computes d=(p−1)(m+1) at infinity, giving d=4 for p=2,m=3.
The same concrete family has e=p, so the characteristic-two cubic gives d=4>e−1=1.
The wild calibration has an actual unique degree-one place above infinity, not a conditional computation at a possibly nonexistent place.
The actual y²−y=x³ field in characteristic two has genus one, compatible with different degree four and incompatible with the naive tame count.
The native y²=x⁵−1 field has different degree six under the explicit characteristic exclusions.
The genus-two different is the distinct finite branch places plus a degree-one infinity place; the finite contribution has degree five independently of splitting.

`WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)` correctly packages a scalar value and an E-valued gradient using the Euclidean product norm. On a real inner-product space its squared norm is |u|²+‖g‖². This is the fibre used by the [Sobolev graph construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Basic.lean#L571); no differentiability condition belongs to the fibre itself. The [native p=2 norm check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Basic.lean#L239) passes, recovering [Evans’s H¹ norm, §5.2.2](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=251). For p≠2 this convention gives an equivalent classical Sobolev norm. LaneA.1 has no separate fibre Check.
At exponent2 the L² norm of this fibre gives exactly the sum of squared value and gradient norms.

This is exactly the Bochner space `Lp (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)) p (μ.restrict Ω)`: value-gradient fields modulo equality almost everywhere on Ω. It is the ambient space; the weak integration-by-parts relation is imposed separately. That agrees with [Evans, §5.2.2](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=251), which identifies Sobolev functions almost everywhere. The [coordinate-extensionality check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Basic.lean#L192) and [H¹ norm identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Basic.lean#L239) pass. Restricting the measure correctly ignores values outside Ω; the empty domain yields the zero Lp space. The raw exponent generality follows Mathlib, while Sobolev consumers require p≥1.
Equality of both Lp coordinate classes determines the ambient jet, independently of representatives.
The p=2 norm has the intended Hilbert normalization.

`W1p.valueL u` returns the scalar Lp class of the Sobolev jet, matching the almost-everywhere convention in [Evans, §5.2.2](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=251). It is a class, not a privileged pointwise representative. The [a.e. coordinate formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Basic.lean#L423) passes, and the [constructor check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Basic.lean#L596) recovers exactly the supplied value class. The definition preserves the domain’s restricted measure and p≥1. The projection remains meaningful in the documented generalized graph space; classical weak-derivative identification is a separate finite-dimensional theorem. No standalone LaneA.1 Check is assigned to this projection.
The projection agrees almost everywhere with the first coordinate of the underlying jet.
Constructing a Sobolev element from a value and weak gradient returns the original Lp value class.

The definition reads the jet’s E-valued Lp component. In finite dimension, the published [weak-derivative identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Basic.lean#L610) proves that its inner product with each direction is the distributional derivative of the value, exactly [Evans’s weak-gradient convention, §5.2.1](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=249). The [coordinate formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Basic.lean#L468) is correctly only almost everywhere. Thus it does not differentiate an arbitrary chosen Lp representative pointwise. The broader graph-space definition documents its infinite-dimensional degeneracy; the classical identification uses the needed finite-dimensional hypothesis. Both native checks pass; no separate projection Check is specified in LaneA.1.
The recorded gradient represents the actual weak Fréchet derivative of the value in the classical finite-dimensional setting.
The Lp gradient agrees almost everywhere with the second jet coordinate.

`(w1p0Submodule μ Ω p).toSubmodule` gives the type of Sobolev elements in the closure of compactly supported smooth jets, with the inherited graph norm. This is [Evans’s definition of `W^{k,p}_0`, §5.2.2](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=251), specialized to first order. The [closure identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Zero.lean#L138) and [test-function membership](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Zero.lean#L144) pass. No boundary regularity is required for this definition. It also makes sense at p=∞, without claiming smooth density in the whole Sobolev space or equality with a trace kernel there. LaneA.2’s closure clause is satisfied; those comparison theorems are separate.
The underlying set is precisely the closure of the set of embedded test-function jets.
Every genuine compactly supported smooth function lies in the zero-boundary subspace.

The definition takes the topological closure of the linear range `φ ↦ (φ,∇φ)` inside `W^{1,p}(Ω)`, exactly the [C∞c-closure definition in Evans, §5.2.2](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=251). The [set-level closure formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Zero.lean#L138) and [minimality theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Zero.lean#L149) pass. The embedding uses the actual classical gradient and is injective. Consequently this closed subspace expresses homogeneous Dirichlet data without assuming a boundary trace or boundary regularity. The choice of an equivalent graph norm does not change its closure. LaneA.2 specifies this construction; Meyers–Serrin and trace identification remain separate claims.
The ClosedSubmodule carrier is the ordinary topological closure of the embedded test-function range.
Every closed set containing all embedded test functions contains the constructed subspace, verifying the intended smallest-closed-set characterization.

This continuous linear map is the inclusion `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)`→`W^{1,p}(Ω)`, followed by the value projection into Lp(Ω). It is the canonical map for the [closure-defined Sobolev space in Evans, §5.2.2](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=251). The [evaluation check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Zero.lean#L178) preserves exactly the underlying value class. The [dense-range theorem at p=2](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Zero.lean#L183) passes and confirms that this is not a zero map on nontrivial domains. Neither surjectivity nor a pointwise boundary restriction is claimed. No additional LaneA.2 Check is attached to this inherited projection.
Restricting the Sobolev value map preserves the original value class.
The actual value projection from H1_0 has dense range in L², via the embedded test functions.

The predicate requires local integrability of u and u′, completeness of the codomain, and ∫(∂ᵥφ)u=−∫φu′ for every smooth test supported compactly in Ω. For Haar measure this is [Evans’s weak derivative, §5.2.1](https://math24.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/partial-differential-equations-by-evans.pdf#page=249). Completeness and integrability exclude Lean’s default-valued integrals. For arbitrary μ the docstring correctly specifies a relative adjoint relation instead.
